cases.name: an empty object
cases.why: An empty object is `{}`.

cases.name: an empty array
cases.why: An empty array is `[]`.

cases.name: null at the top level
cases.why: A value that is not an object or an array is written as JSON writes it.

cases.name: a string at the top level
cases.why: A value that is not an object or an array is written as JSON writes it.

cases.name: white space between tokens is removed
cases.why: The output has no white space outside strings.

cases.name: keys are sorted
cases.why: The keys of an object are written in ascending order.

cases.name: keys are sorted at every depth and arrays keep their order
cases.why: Sorting applies to every object. It never reorders an array.

cases.name: empty containers inside containers
cases.why: Empty objects and arrays are written at any depth.

cases.name: keys are compared by code unit, so uppercase sorts before lowercase
cases.why: The order is by UTF-16 code unit, not by any alphabet: `1` < `B` < `_` < `a`.

cases.name: a key that is a prefix of another sorts first
cases.why: The empty key sorts before every other key.

cases.name: keys that look like numbers are sorted as strings
cases.why: `10` sorts before `9`.

cases.name: keys are sorted by UTF-16 code unit, not by code point
cases.why: U+1F600 is the surrogate pair D83D DE00 in UTF-16, so it sorts before U+FF5E. Sorted by code point or by UTF-8 byte, U+FF5E would sort first.

cases.name: a repeated key keeps the last value
cases.why: The parser decides: the later member replaces the earlier one.

cases.name: characters outside ASCII are written as they are
cases.why: Only the characters that JSON requires are escaped.

cases.name: a character outside the Basic Multilingual Plane is written as it is
cases.why: A valid surrogate pair is written as the character, which is four bytes in UTF-8.

cases.name: <, >, and & are not escaped
cases.why: Characters that are special in HTML are written as they are.

cases.name: U+2028 and U+2029 are not escaped
cases.why: The two line separator characters are written as they are.

cases.name: the quote and the backslash are escaped
cases.why: `"` is written as `\"` and `\` as `\\`.

cases.name: the slash is not escaped
cases.why: An escaped `/` in the input is written as `/`.

cases.name: control characters with a short escape use it
cases.why: U+0008, U+0009, U+000A, U+000C, and U+000D are written as `\b`, `\t`, `\n`, `\f`, and `\r`.

cases.name: other control characters use \u with lowercase hexadecimal
cases.why: Every other character below U+0020 is written as `\u00xx` in lowercase.

cases.name: U+007F is not escaped
cases.why: Only the characters below U+0020 are control characters for this purpose.

cases.name: a lone high surrogate is escaped
cases.why: A surrogate with no partner is written as a `\u` escape in lowercase.

cases.name: a lone low surrogate is escaped
cases.why: A surrogate with no partner is written as a `\u` escape in lowercase.

cases.name: surrogates in the wrong order are both escaped
cases.why: A low surrogate followed by a high surrogate is not a pair.

cases.name: 1.0 is written as 1
cases.why: A number with a zero fraction is written as an integer.

cases.name: 2.50 is written as 2.5
cases.why: Trailing zeros of a fraction are dropped.

cases.name: -0 is written as 0
cases.why: Negative zero loses its sign.

cases.name: an exponent is expanded below 1e21
cases.why: `1E3` is written as `1000`.

cases.name: 1e20 is written in full
cases.why: The largest power of ten that is written without an exponent.

cases.name: 1e21 is written as 1e+21
cases.why: From 1e21 on, a number is written with an exponent and an explicit `+`.

cases.name: -1e21 is written as -1e+21
cases.why: The limit of 1e21 is a limit on the absolute value.

cases.name: 0.000001 is written in full
cases.why: The smallest power of ten that is written without an exponent.

cases.name: 0.0000001 is written as 1e-7
cases.why: Below 1e-6, a number is written with an exponent.

cases.name: -0.0000001 is written as -1e-7
cases.why: The limit of 1e-6 is a limit on the absolute value.

cases.name: a large integer is rounded to the nearest double
cases.why: Every number is an IEEE 754 double. 9007199254740993 is not one, so it becomes 9007199254740992.

cases.name: a 21-digit integer is rounded and written in full
cases.why: The shortest digits that identify the double are written, then zeros.

cases.name: extra digits of a fraction are dropped
cases.why: The shortest digits that identify the double are written.

cases.name: the smallest double
cases.why: A subnormal number is written with an exponent.

cases.name: a number too large for a double is written as null
cases.why: 1e400 is read as infinity, and infinity is written as `null`.

cases.name: numbers inside an array
cases.why: Number rules apply at any depth.

description: JSON texts and their canonical form. `sha256` is the SHA-256 of the UTF-8 bytes of `canonical`, in lowercase hexadecimal.
